overall: The Board violated the law by not recording the time and date its October 30, 2014 meeting notice was posted, but the harm was minimal because posting was well over 48 hours ahead. No executive session was held, so the litigation-topic complaint and the response-timeliness complaint were not violations. No further relief ordered.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the notice for the October 30, 2014 meeting did not show the time it was posted; the AG also noted the 48-hour posting rule.
Complaint alleged the notice's 'Executive Session - (Pending Litigation)' entry lacked enough detail about the litigation matter.
allegations.key_passage: Because the Board never entered into executive session during its October 30, 2014 meeting, and thus there was no discussion requiring more specific notice than what was provided, we find that the Board did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board's written response to the complaint was not timely.
allegations.key_passage: We find that this was timely. See G.L. c. 30A, § 23(b); 940 CMR 29.05(5).
